evidence: Cic. Dom. 122: omnia sollemnibus verbīs dīcere (Lewis & Short)
Cic. de Or. 3.197: sollemnēs epulae (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: First “yearly”, of fixed religious rites; then of anything done with its proper ceremony, a festival, a feast, a form of words, a wedding (sollemne nūptiārum, Suet.); after Augustus also “usual, customary” (Lewis & Short). Sollemne as a noun is a rite or ceremony.

phrases.latin: īte fēlīcēs, ait; celebrāte sine mē cursū sollemnem diem
phrases.english: “Go, and good luck to you,” he said; “keep the festival day with a race, without me”

sources: Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-phaedrus), checked against the editions named there.
